shots.line: This guy took a hundred and fifty thousand dollars from a fast food giant... and it was completely legal.
shots.scene: sunset: a student in a beanie walks out of a burger restaurant toward us holding one paper cup, hundred-dollar bills fluttering around him, BURGERS pole sign glowing; a money counter races to $150,000

shots.line: Meet Chris. A broke computer science student. His dream: one semester in Japan. His bank account: forty-two dollars.
shots.scene: a cosy dorm room at sunset: Chris types at his desk; the camera drifts to a JAPAN poster with Mt Fuji; his phone shows a balance of $42

shots.line: Then a burger chain launched a contest. Collect the codes on your cups... win up to a million dollars.
shots.scene: golden hour: the burger restaurant is packed, a line of people with cups out the door, a big yellow banner WIN $1,000,000, cars passing; the camera glides from the street up to the banner and pole sign

shots.line: Chris didn't buy a single burger. Instead, he went to the cleaners behind every restaurant in town... and offered to take their trash. For free.
shots.scene: sunset: Chris walks right past the queue without buying, rounds the corner into the back alley full of dumpsters and black trash bags, and offers two cleaners to take their trash — they shrug and hand it over

shots.line: Night after night, he dragged home thousands of dirty cups.
shots.scene: night under street lamps: Chris drags three bulging black trash bags along the sidewalk past closed shops; moon and stars, a passing car

shots.line: He typed every single code into a program he wrote himself. Days passed. Nothing. Then, at two a.m., his screen turned green.
shots.scene: night dorm buried in thousands of cups; Chris types codes into his own program, codes scroll red; days pass; at 2 a.m. the monitor turns bright green and he jumps up

shots.line: The codes weren't random. They followed a formula... based on the print date and the factory number.
shots.scene: tech-grid graphic: a giant cup turns, its code 0417-F23-8812 splits into parts: PRINT DATE and FACTORY # — glowing formula lines connect them

shots.line: Chris could now predict which boxes, on which days, carried the big winners.
shots.scene: map graphic: from a factory, delivery trucks drive to restaurant pins; certain boxes light up gold with $$$ — BOX 14 · TUESDAY

shots.line: He drove to those restaurants... and bought one single cup each time.
shots.scene: sunset: Chris's car pulls into the burger lot; he walks out of the door with ONE cup raised, grinning

shots.line: Two weeks later: a hundred and fifty thousand dollars.
shots.scene: golden sunset: hundred-dollar bills rain over the street, Chris jumps with joy in front of the burger sign — $150,000 in two weeks

shots.line: No rules broken. He just read the system... and booked his flight to Tokyo.
shots.scene: sunset over Tokyo: a jet glides past toward snowy Mt Fuji; cherry blossoms drift; Chris stands under a sakura tree with his backpack, smiling — NO RULES BROKEN
